sections.html:
Gage County lies along Nebraska's southern edge, touching Kansas, with Beatrice as the county seat. The 2020 census counted 21,704 residents and the 2025 estimate is 21,711, so the population has held steady. The county has three cities, Beatrice, Blue Springs and Wymore, plus nine villages. Lincoln is the nearest large city for much of the county, about 40 miles north of Beatrice.

Housing units numbered 10,327 in 2020, with 10.1% vacant. Nearly three in ten occupied homes were rented, so landlords are a real part of the seller pool. A county settled this early describes parcels by legal description, and a title company will want to read that description and the recorded history before closing.

sections.h2: How the assessor values a home
sections.html:
The assessor values most homes at replacement cost new less depreciation, adds land, then tests the results against sales within defined market areas. The target for residential and commercial property is 92 to 100 percent of market value, and for agricultural land it's 69 to 75 percent.

Residential values rely on a two-year sales study, agricultural and commercial values on three years, and the study period ends June 30 of the preceding year. State law has the office review each property at least every six years. Field staff drive county vehicles and wear name badges and bright green vests.

  • A market neighborhood can include as many as 500 homes, so values are set by group, not by one sale.
  • Commercial property is often valued by an income approach, and income information sent to the office stays confidential.
  • Your mailing address for tax statements comes from line 19 of the Form 521 transfer statement filed with your deed.
  • Greenbelt status for qualifying farmland requires Form 456 before August 1.

You protest the valuation, never the tax itself. File Form 422 in triplicate with the County Board of Equalization at the county clerk's office, 612 Grant Street in Beatrice. Real property protests are due on or before June 30 and personal property protests by May 1. A protest that omits the requested value and the reasons can be dismissed.

The assessor's office suggests first asking an appraiser to explain how your value was reached, which gives the office a chance to fix errors. After a hearing, the board notifies you of its decision within seven days. A further appeal goes to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission within 30 days after the board adjourns, with July 25 deemed the adjournment date for the June 1 to July 25 session.

Useful evidence shows that the assessor valued your property above market value or out of line with similar properties.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and ways to pay
sections.html:
Real estate and personal property taxes are due December 31. The first half turns delinquent the following May 1 and the second half on September 1, and a 14 percent statutory rate applies to delinquencies. Notices are mailed in December.

Payment methodFee
Online at nto.us, card2.49 percent convenience fee

The treasurer's office phone is (402) 223-1319. If your address is wrong, call or use the county's change of address form.

Mobile homes follow a few extra rules. The county doesn't prorate taxes on a sold mobile home, so buyer and seller must split them. A moving permit isn't issued until taxes are paid to date, and moving without that step is a class four misdemeanor. If the new owner never files forms 521 and 402, the tax statement stays in the seller's name.

sections.h2: How the Gage County tax sale works
sections.html:
The treasurer holds a public tax sale each March in the district courtroom on the third floor of the courthouse, starting at 9:00 a.m. Delinquent parcels are advertised for three consecutive weeks in February in the Beatrice Daily Sun.

Bidders register in advance, pay a $25 registration fee, and take turns choosing parcels round-robin under Nebraska statute 77-1807. A buyer gets a tax lien, not the property. A certificate that isn't redeemed within three years opens the way to foreclosure, with strict notice deadlines before three years and nine months. Redemption pays the buyer 14 percent interest, and purchasers add an automatic $150 administrative fee for serving notice on the owner, which the owner pays at redemption.

Parcels in bankruptcy or owned by government entities are left out of the sale. Owners who want to avoid the notice step and extra fees usually clear the balance or sell before the February advertising run.

Homestead exemption applicants, generally owners over 65 and certain disabled people, must file between February 1 and June 30 every year in the assessor's office. You lose the exemption if you sell or leave the home before August 15, though if you buy another Nebraska home before that date you can file a transfer statement to move it.

At closing, Nebraska's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 per $1,000 of value for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026, paid by the seller as grantor. Zoning and building permits, including setbacks, are checked by legal description and address with county planning, and a permit application needs two identical sets of plans.

If you've added a garage, deck or finished space, gather those permits before you list. A buyer's title company or lender may ask for them.

sections.h2: Selling a Gage County house with taxes owed
sections.html:
You can sell a house that's on the tax sale list, as long as delinquent taxes and charges are paid at closing. If a certificate has already been sold, you also owe the buyer's interest and the $150 service fee to redeem. The title company requests the payoff from the treasurer and pays it from your proceeds.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Gage County address and explain how an as-is offer would work. A cash sale skips showings and lender appraisals, which helps when a February advertising date is close.

faqs.q: When are Gage County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31. The first half is delinquent the following May 1 and the second half the following September 1, with a 14 percent statutory rate on delinquencies.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Gage County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Only the valuation, not the bill. File Form 422 with the county clerk in Beatrice by June 30 for real property, stating the value you want and why.

faqs.q: What fees apply when paying Gage County taxes by card?
faqs.a: A 2.49 percent convenience fee for credit or debit cards, and $1.75 for an e-check. Real estate taxes can be paid online at nto.us.

faqs.q: Does Gage County prorate taxes when a mobile home is sold?
faqs.a: No. Buyer and seller split them. The new owner must also file forms 521 and 402 with the assessor, or the bill stays in the seller's name.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gage County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes, if the delinquent taxes and charges are paid at closing. If a certificate has already been sold, the owner also owes the buyer's interest and a $150 service fee to redeem.
